papers.title_en: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals
papers.authors: Yanlong Chen, Simone Benatti, Luca Benini, Cuntai Guan, Yawei Li
papers.evidence: 面向EEG的小波时频令牌化与通道嵌入
papers.tldr: 针对生物信号基础模型token序列长、跨导联与采样率适配难的问题，PhysioWave-T提出动态尺度折叠，在token化前重组合并小波子带，将序列长度从(J+1)CS压缩到CS。每模态用单一Transformer配合路由前端和通道名嵌入，未见配置以轻量适配器复用骨干。EEG任务中延迟降4.0–7.2倍、峰值内存降6.8–12.7倍且无精度损失，并在多基准领先；RALF融合进一步提升可穿戴癫痫检测。
papers.abstract_en: We present PhysioWave-T, a token-efficient wavelet foundation model family for EEG, ECG, and sEMG. Dynamic scale folding recombines J+1 wavelet subbands prior to tokenization, compressing sequence length from (J+1)CS to CS tokens for J levels, C channels, and S temporal patches. Route-specific front ends and learned channel-name embeddings allow one Transformer per modality to handle diverse montages and sampling rates, while unseen setups reuse the backbone via lightweight adapters. We pre-train a 30M-parameter EEG model on over 15M windows (19--128 channels), alongside ECG (30M) and sEMG (12M) encoders. Across four EEG routes, scale folding cuts Transformer latency by 4.0--7.2x and peak memory by 6.8--12.7x over scale expansion without accuracy loss. Our EEG encoder leads 8 of 9 metrics against BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGPT, and surpasses LUNA-L on wearable seizure detection with fewer parameters. Reliability-aware latent fusion (RALF) further integrates summary tokens from independently pre-trained encoders via sample-adaptive weights. On SeizeIT2, RALF raises event sensitivity at 11 false alarms/h from 61.4% to 74.4% and window AUPRC from 0.321 to 0.399 over the best unimodal baseline, outperforming weighted-logit and concatenation fusion across all variants. PhysioWave-T also achieves state-of-the-art sEMG accuracies and top macro-F1 on PTB-XL Super and Chapman-Shaoxing. Code and models: https://github.com/ForeverBlue816/PhysioWave.

papers.title_en: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
papers.evidence: 将EEG渲染为尺度图与通道行以获可迁移表征
papers.tldr: EEG基础模型冻结特征迁移不稳定，扩大模型或数据也未必改善。SeeEEG将各EEG通道渲染为图像行（波形或时频图），只学习显示参数并冻结视觉主干。在8个临床、睡眠、情感和脑机接口数据集上，冻结DINOv3的SeeEEG平衡准确率全面超过7个EEG基础模型，kappa或AUROC平均排名1.3，优于REVE的2.9。显示参数还能零优化迁移到V-JEPA 2.1，说明读取EEG的能力来自视觉预训练。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fall within individual tokens. The montage, filtering, and contrast parameters of this display are initialized from a standard clinical montage and optimized with the task loss through the frozen backbone, which amounts to at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view. We compare SeeEEG with seven EEG foundation models on eight clinical, sleep, affective, and brain-computer interface datasets, with every encoder frozen and paired with identical readout heads. With a frozen DINOv3 ViT-B, SeeEEG outperforms every EEG foundation model in balanced accuracy on all eight datasets and reaches a mean rank of 1.3 in Cohen kappa or AUROC, compared with 2.9 for the strongest baseline, REVE. The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of the eight datasets. Replacing DINOv3 with a randomly initialized ViT-B lowers the score by 15.2 points on average, so the ability to read rendered EEG comes from visual pretraining.

papers.title_en: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
papers.evidence: 面向脑电分类的标签噪声检测与校正
papers.tldr: 睡眠分期模型受人工标注噪声与评分者分歧制约。本文提出只在训练阶段使用的 LLM 辅助标签清洗流程：先用 TinySleepNet 的 SoftMax 置信度筛出低置信 epoch，再交由 LLaMA 3.1 结合频谱特征与序列上下文、按 AASM 规则判定为可靠或可疑，剔除可疑样本后重训。Sleep-EDF 上 20 折交叉验证准确率由 81.8% 升至 84.6%，Macro F1 由 75.6% 升至 77.4%，REM 提升明显；推理端仍保留 1.3M 参数的轻量模型。
papers.abstract_en: Automatic sleep stage classification from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is a critical task in clinical sleep medicine. While deep learning models have shown promising results in this domain, their performance is fundamentally constrained by the quality of training labels, which human experts manually annotate and that are subject to inter-rater disagreement and systematic labeling errors. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-assisted label-noise filtering pipeline that operates exclusively during training to identify and remove unreliable sleep-stage annotations before retraining the classifier. Specifically, TinySleepNet is first trained on the original dataset to extract per-epoch SoftMax confidence scores, then low-confidence epochs are submitted to LLaMA 3.1 along with their EEG spectral features and surrounding sequence context. The LLM evaluates each epoch against AASM sleep-scoring guidelines and assigns a verdict of RELIABLE or SUSPICIOUS. Suspicious epochs are removed from the training set, and TinySleepNet is retrained on the cleaned data. Evaluated on the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset using 20-fold cross-validation, our method improves overall accuracy from 81.8% to 84.6% and Macro F1-score from 75.6% to 77.4%, with particularly notable gains in REM detection. Crucially, because the LLM operates only during training, the lightweight TinySleepNet architecture (1.3M parameters) is preserved at inference, making the proposed pipeline suitable for real-time, wearable sleep monitoring applications.

papers.title_en: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.authors: SuGil Choi, Mooseop Kim, Chi Yoon Jeong
papers.evidence: 相关性感知的脑电基础模型学习泛化表征
papers.tldr: 现有EEG基础模型多采用随机掩码重建，且Transformer位置编码未充分适配脑电通道相关性，限制表征学习。CABrain用基于图卷积的条件位置编码显式建模通道相关，并引入自适应掩码调节重建难度。在十个基准数据集上，两种策略单独或组合均达SOTA或具竞争力。该工作首次将图表示融入条件位置编码与自适应掩码的EEG基础模型预训练。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models have emerged as promising paradigms for decoding brain activity through large-scale self-supervised pretraining. Notably, most existing approaches employ masked patch reconstruction, in which randomly selected EEG patches are masked and recovered by the network. However, purely random masking may limit representation learning as informative patches from highly correlated channels often remain unmasked, causing the network to underutilize weakly correlated channels or serial dependencies. Furthermore, because these models are typically based on transformer architectures, their performance is influenced by the choice of positional encoding. Although positional encoding has been extensively explored in natural language processing and computer vision, few studies have adapted it to the unique characteristics of EEG signals. To address these limitations, this study introduces a conditional positional encoding method based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to explicitly model inter-channel correlations, along with an adaptive masking strategy that enhances representation learning by modulating the difficulty of masked patch reconstruction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to integrate graph-based representations into conditional positional encoding and introduce adaptive masking within EEG foundation model pretraining. Experimental results on ten benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCN-based positional encoding and adaptive masking strategies, both individually and in combination, achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance, highlighting their effectiveness in EEG foundation modeling.

papers.title_en: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
papers.authors: Minyu Zhou, Yajing Wu, Yongqiang Tang, Wang Jia, Wensheng Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向可泛化脑机接口的尺度一致脑电表征学习
papers.tldr: 针对EEG基础模型中多尺度特征与原始信号尺度对应关系不明确、自监督目标与多尺度输入不匹配的问题，ScaleBrain提出尺度一致预训练框架。它用不同时间跨度且共享时间锚点的分析窗进行多尺度分词，并配合尺度特定重建，使各时间分辨率都获得充分监督。模型还引入轴向时空注意力融合多尺度表征。在六个公开BCI基准上对比12个基线，ScaleBrain以仅5.0M参数在五个数据集取得最高平均平衡准确率，另一个排名第三。
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models pre-trained on large unlabeled electroencephalography (EEG) corpora have emerged as a transformative paradigm for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. Recent EEG foundation models have shown that multi-scale representations derived from fixed-length patches can improve EEG representation learning. Existing frameworks commonly construct temporal scales through feature-level operations. However, these operations leave the correspondence between learned features and scale-specific characteristics of the original EEG signals implicit. Moreover, when the self-supervised objective is not aligned with the multi-scale input representations, information at some temporal scales may receive insufficient supervision during pre-training. In light of this, we propose ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework that explicitly coordinates multi-scale representations of EEG from both the model input and optimization objective sides. Specifically, ScaleBrain introduces multi-scale EEG tokenization to represent the same EEG segment through analysis windows with different temporal spans and shared temporal anchors, and pairs these representations with scale-specific reconstruction to align with the multi-scale input structure and provide supervision across temporal resolutions during self-supervised learning. We further develop an axial spatio-temporal attention mechanism to contextualize the fused multi-scale representation along spatial and temporal dimensions. Extensive evaluations on six public BCI benchmarks against 12 representative baselines show that ScaleBrain achieves the highest mean Balanced Accuracy on five datasets and ranks third on the remaining one, with only 5.0M parameters, demonstrating strong performance and favorable parameter efficiency.
